t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Pirate Radio
d: Krang plots to take city by luring citizens into an inter­dimensional "Krang's Chasm" at sea by inserting Shredder in place of DJ. Dickie Bark as a Pied Piper on steamship radio station.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Raphael, the Turtle of a Thousand Faces
st: Raphael, the Turtle of a Thousand Faces
d: Raphael disguises himself as Mad Dog McNutt, who is planning a heist of the Natural History museum.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Leonardo, the Renaissance Turtle
d: Professor Mindbender fools the Mayor into installing Lex, a supercop robot, to clean up crime, but rewires him to arrest practically the whole city.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Zach and the Alien Invaders
d: Zach's over-active imagination has him seeing Aliens everywhere. Sent to Military School, he discovers actual Aliens posing as officers.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Welcome Back, Polarisoids!
d: The Polarisoids return to Earth unwittingly invited by Krang, bringing to life the alien Creatures caught as images on tape as a distraction so Krang can break into the city's computer systems.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Planet of the Turtleloids: Part 1
d: Krang and Shredder transport to the City Wild Animal Park with Bebop and Rocksteady to create an army of Mutants from the animals there.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Rock Around the Block
d: Krang summons General Tragg from the Dimension X to keep the Turtles busy while Shredder places a remote control transmitter upon a rocket ship preparing to launch a satellite with a new super laser.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Krangenstein Lives
d: Under the Arctic Ocean Krang is tuning up his Robotic Body. While no one is looking, Bebop and Rocksteady inadvertently destroy an important computer chip and surreptitiously replace it with one from a video game.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Super Irma
d: While the Turtles are busy trying to decide what costumes to wear to this year's Channel Six Halloween party, April and Irma are doing a story on the reverse polarity magnet at Magno-Dyne Labs.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Adventures in Turtle-Sitting
d: While Splinter is away on meditative satori, Donatello sets his sights on solving world hunger. He invents the food revivafiver, a device designed to reverse the aging process of food.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Sword of Yurikawa
d: Krang plans to blow up the Tri-State Bridge just as a convoy of trucks carrying a rare form of toxic waste passes overhead.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Return of the Turtleoid
d: The Turtles go to the Top Notch Scientific Corporation to stand guard over the sonic disintegrator.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Shreeka's Revenge
d: Shreeka, an alien with an attitude and a vendetta against Krang, after having spent eons tracking him down, has finally found him.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Too Hot to Handle
d: Donatello tells the other three Turtles that, based on his calculations, the Earth has changed its orbit and is heading for the Sun.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Nightmare in the Lair
d: Down in the sewers, while Michelangelo, Leonardo, and Raphael are watching yet another cheesy sci-fi film, Donatello is busy building the dream-o-vision.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Phantom of the Sewers
d: After another night's performance of the robotic Willie Wombat Revue at the Willie Wombat Revue Theatre, a mysterious figure, wearing a long black cape, black fedora, white face mask, and known only as the Phantom, makes an appearance.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Leonardo is Missing
d: When Donatello, Michelangelo, and Raphael return from the video arcade they discover that Donatello's lab is in disarray and Leonardo is missing.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Snakes Alive!
d: While practicing their martial arts, Leonardo tells Splinter that he is convinced that there is one combat maneuver he has yet to teach the Turtles.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Polly Wanna Pizza
d: Michelangelo returns from his sojourn to the pet shop with a monkey named Clyde. After only a few minutes with the undisciplined pet Leonardo, Donatello and Raphael demand that it be returned to the pet shop.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Mr. Nice Guy
d: Burne assigns April a story reporting on the increase in urban crime. The only problem is that urban crime is decreasing.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Sleuth on the Loose
d: While the Turtles are watching their favorite TV show April interrupts the broadcast with a special bulletin about a break-in at Dynamic Science Labs.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Rust Never Sleeps
d: Krang works on an oxidizer rocket with enough power to blast the Technodrome to Earth, but something goes wrong, and instead of thrust, the device grows rust.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): A Real Snow Job
d: The Turtles are holidaying in the Alps, as Splinter goes off to a nearby mountain to meditate. April is in an Alpine village with Irma when she notices the ice and snow melting, unusual for this time of year.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Venice on the Half-Shell
d: Krang decides to use a hydrofluxer device to flood Venice, holding it for ransom.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Artless
d: Two snobbish art-collecting aliens arrive in Florence and begin stealing great works of art.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Ring of Fire
d: Krang sends Shredder to set up a special lens that will focus the sun's rays to create a devastating heat ray.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Irish Jig Is Up
d: Krang and Shredder decide to use Ireland as their base for the Technodrome. With a device called the Rainbow Trans-Charmer, the villains intend to turn harmless little creatures like sheep and rabbits into slavering beasts.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Shredder's New Sword
d: In Dimension X Krang is using a long-range scanner and discovers a rare metal buried in a ruined castle in England. The metal turns out to be King Arthur's legendary sword, Excalibur.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Lost Queen of Atlantis
d: Shredder, Rocksteady and Bebop are searching for a valuable energy source in Athens and discover that it is April's new necklace.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Turtles on the Orient Express
d: April is covering the revival of the Orient Express. Shredder is on the train with Rocksteady and Bebop carrying the supercharger, a device to accelerate the train to super speed.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): April Gets in Dutch
d: April is covering the showing of the world-famed Duchess Diamond. Krang wants the diamond, a flawless stone, to focus the rays on his laser dimension blade.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Northern Lights Out
d: Eric Red seizes both April and Professor Swenson's map to the underground volcanoes in Scandinavia to tap into the molten energy and melt the polar ice caps.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Elementary, My Dear Turtle
d: The Turtles are in England, when they are taken back to the past, via an experimental atomic clock and must team up with Sherlock Holmes and Doctor Watson in order to get the clock back and return to the present.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Night of the Dark Turtle
d: When Donatello receives a jolt of electrical energy, he undergoes a radical personality transformation, turning into 'The Dark Turtle', a psychotic caped crimefighter on a mission of revenge against Shredder!

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Starchild
d: The Turtles face a crisis of galactic proportions when they must play babysitter to an alien infant with incredible powers.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): The Legend of Koji
d: The Turtles take an incredible trip back in time when they follow Shredder back to 16th Century Japan, where they join forces with Splinter's ancestor, the youthful samurai koji, and help him found the Foot Clan.

t: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987): Convicts from Dimension X
d: Donatello, tinkering with his InterDimensional Early Warning System device, accidently frees two vicious convicts from their maximum security cell on Dimension X, bringing them to earth.
